open_questions: Mass measurement (RV/TV) still needed to rule out a small-star grazing blend missed by depth alone.
Why centroid_all did not run limits independent confirmation that the dip is on-target in all sectors.
dossier.public_summary: The dip is centered on the target star and other stars nearby cannot produce a dip that deep. The large change in depth between sectors comes from one TESS pipeline with four bad transits; the higher-quality pipelines show a steady shallow dip. Its size and duration match a small planet around a K-dwarf, with no sign of an eclipsing binary.

reasons.why: Centroid in sector 74 puts the dip on the target; the closest star that could cause it is 21.5 arcsec away needing 0.2218 eclipse and is 5.4 sigma from the centroid.
Extreme sector depth scatter is explained fully by the QLP sector 79 outlier (14955 ppm vs 0 ppm elsewhere), not contamination: SPOC products are steady.
reasons.value: p_constant_all: 1.796e-95, verdict: differs_by_source (QLP 14955 +/- 694 ppm vs SPOC 2-min 88 +/- 57 ppm vs TESS-SPOC 49 +/- 49 ppm)

reasons.why: Signal is carried by 3 QLP pipeline transits that are 25-48 sigma too deep and one 4-minute transit, classic bad photometry systematics rather than an astrophysical depth change.
reasons.value: p_consistent: 0.0, share_of_top_3: 0.869, outliers 20331, 15692, 12761, 11044 ppm, single 4-min transit 3457.167

reasons.why: No neighbour within 1 TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can plausibly cause a 732 ppm dip and folded SPOC secondary and odd/even signals are consistent with systematics, not a stellar companion.
reasons.value: plausible_within_1px: 0, secondary.snr: 5.56 at phase 0.7778 depth_ppm:157.2, secondary_over_bump:1.163, odd_even.diff_sigma:3.355

reasons.why: When the QLP outlier is excluded SPOC depth ~100 ppm implies an ~2 Earth-radius planet duration for a 0.75 Rsun K dwarf, flat-bottom shape and centric impact; Gaia radii agree.
